description: Web side of the image queue: webapp.py gains write access to the queue directory only (MAX_CONTENT_LENGTH cap, GET/POST /upload with REAL ffmpeg conversion and atomic publish, a queue-listing helper, VSMP_QUEUE config pointing at the SAME dir the player reads, an optional GET /queue.json, and a clearly-marked DISABLED auth hook), a new phone-friendly templates/upload.html landing page with explainers + queue length + estimated wait + post-upload landed position, a link to it from status.html, and reuse of style.css classes. Plus webapp tests exercising upload -> real ffmpeg convert -> atomic publish, a HEIC fixture, and a concurrent-upload check. Depends on FEAT-001 (uses vsmp.convert_image_to_panel_png, vsmp.QUEUE_DIR, and the queue/.incoming/.showing layout and FIFO naming contract).
steps: In webapp.py set app.config['MAX_CONTENT_LENGTH'] = 16 * 1024 * 1024 (so an oversized phone photo returns a clean 413 instead of exhausting RAM). Add QUEUE_PATH = os.environ.get('VSMP_QUEUE', vsmp.QUEUE_DIR) — the SAME directory the player reads. Keep webapp.py driver-free: it must continue to import vsmp only for read-only helpers plus the new convert_image_to_panel_png, and must never import epd.

Add a generated-filename helper producing sortable unique names '{ms:013d}_{counter:06d}_{rand6}.png' (milliseconds since epoch, a per-process counter, 6 hex random chars) so lexical sort == arrival order and two uploaders in the same millisecond cannot collide. Store under this generated name only; never trust the uploaded filename (use werkzeug.utils.secure_filename solely if displaying the user's original name).

Add a queue-listing helper list_queue_summary(queue_path) returning the ordered list of published names, the length (count queue_path/*.png ONLY — never .incoming/ or .showing/), and the estimated wait = length * vsmp.FRAME_INTERVAL_S. This is the single formula the page and /queue.json both use. The count is an unlocked live snapshot by design (the player may claim the oldest file between read and render), which keeps the webapp's no-lock contract.
Add GET /upload: render templates/upload.html with the queue summary (length, ordered list, estimated wait).

Add POST /upload: require a file field named 'image' (400 with a readable message if missing); save the raw upload to a temp file under queue/.incoming/, run vsmp.convert_image_to_panel_png(tmp_in, queue/.incoming/<name>.tmp), validate the result is a non-empty PNG by trusting ffmpeg's output rather than the uploaded extension/MIME, then os.rename it into queue/<generated-name>.png (atomic publish on the same filesystem). On any conversion failure, reject with a clear message and write NOTHING into queue/ (clean up temp files). Compute the landed position = 1-based index of the new name in the freshly sorted queue and pass it to the template so the confirmation can say e.g. 'added — 4th in line'. Ensure .incoming/ and .showing/ exist (reuse vsmp.queue_paths or mkdir).
Add optional GET /queue.json returning the same summary (length, ordered names, estimated wait seconds) as JSON.

Add a clearly-marked, DISABLED-by-default auth hook: a @app.before_request handler gated on an env var (e.g. VSMP_UPLOAD_SECRET) that is a no-op unless the var is set, with a comment marking it as the place a shared secret/password slots in (design doc section 6). Leave it off for LAN use.

Create templates/upload.html matching status.html card layout and reusing style.css classes (card, facts, muted, small, state). Put TWO short scannable explainers IN THE TEMPLATE (not in Python): explainer 1 = what the VSMP is (a very slow movie player, one frame every 150s, 24/hour, made to be glanced at); explainer 2 = what happens to an uploaded image and how the queue works (joins a FIFO queue, shown one 150s slot, never interrupts the current image, grayscale + scaled/letterboxed, when the queue is empty the movie resumes). Add the phone-friendly form: method=post action=url_for('upload'), enctype='multipart/form-data', <input type=file name=image accept='image/*' required>, a submit button, and NO capture= attribute (so existing photos can be chosen). Show the queue length and estimated wait prominently (minutes, e.g. 'about 7.5 min'); when the queue is empty show 0 and the message 'Queue is empty — the movie is playing' (the zero count and that message must agree). List the current queue so a visitor sees roughly where their image lands. After a successful upload show the landed-position confirmation. Link back to the status page.

Add a link to /upload from templates/status.html (so the two pages are reachable from each other). Add minimal style.css rules only if genuinely needed for the form/queue list; prefer reusing existing classes.

Add tests/test_webapp.py (register it in the MODULES list in tests/run.py). Use Flask's test client (webapp.app.test_client()) with VSMP_QUEUE pointed at a temp dir under the module's work dir. Assert: POST /upload of a real JPEG and a real PNG each yields exactly ONE finished file in queue/ that opens as exactly 800x480 (Image.open(...).size == (800,480)) and passes the panel size guard (feed it through vsmp.display_on_e_ink against harness.FakeEpd with no exception). HEIC case (phone): generate a .heic fixture via `sips -s format heic <png> --out <heic>` when sips is available, upload it, and assert the same 800x480 result; skip() with a clear reason when sips is unavailable (this ffmpeg decodes HEIC but cannot encode it, and the Pi has no sips). Concurrent-upload check: fire several uploads from threads and assert every file lands with a unique name, the count matches, and a scan of queue/ during publishing never sees a partial/temp file (all temp work lives under .incoming/). Assert the empty-queue listing reports length 0 and the 'movie is playing' wording. Assert a non-image upload is rejected with nothing written to queue/. Conversion must be REAL ffmpeg, never stubbed. Follow the harness NEGATIVE CONTROL and subprocess-timeout conventions. Clean up so repo-cleanliness assertions hold.
Run the suite and confirm green; verify `python3 -c 'import webapp'` still imports without pulling in the epd driver.
acceptance_criteria: `python3 tests/run.py test_webapp` passes: JPEG+PNG uploads each produce exactly one 800x480 grayscale PNG in queue/ that passes the panel size guard; the HEIC upload produces the same (or is cleanly skipped when sips is absent); concurrent uploads all land with unique names and no partial file is ever visible in queue/; the empty-queue listing shows 0 and 'movie is playing'; a non-image is rejected with nothing written.

GET /upload renders the landing page with both explainers, the form (accept='image/*', enctype multipart, no capture=), and the queue length + estimated wait; POST /upload returns a landed-position confirmation.
The queue count reflects only published files in queue/ (never .incoming/ or .showing/), and estimated wait = length * 150s via one shared formula used by the page and /queue.json.
webapp.py never imports the epd driver (`python3 -c 'import webapp'` works on this machine) and its only new privilege is writing to the queue directory.
status.html links to /upload and upload.html links back; existing style.css classes are reused.
The full suite `python3 tests/run.py` stays green and the repo is left clean.
verification: python3 -c "import webapp; print('import ok, no driver'); import sys; assert 'epd.epd7in5_V2_old' not in sys.modules"
findings:
Implemented the web side of the image queue. All three FEAT-002 verification commands pass. Full suite green: 252 passed, 0 failed, 4 skipped (the 4 skips are the pre-existing optional real-movie checks). test_webapp contributes 38 passing assertions, HEIC case ran (sips present on this macOS dev box).

ENVIRONMENT NOTE for later features/CI: Flask/Werkzeug/Pillow were NOT installed on the system python3 (/usr/bin/python3, CommandLineTools) in this worktree, so `python3 tests/run.py` fails at `import flask` out of the box. I created a throwaway venv at /tmp/vsmp-venv and ran the suite with /tmp/vsmp-venv/bin/python (which run.py propagates to submodules via sys.executable). Nothing was installed into the repo and the venv is outside it. To re-run the webapp tests: create a venv, `pip install Flask==3.1.3 Werkzeug==3.1.3 pillow==10.3.0`, then `<venv>/bin/python tests/run.py`. The player-only tests still run on bare python3.

webapp.py contracts a later feature (e.g. FEAT-003 deploy/docs) should build on:
- app.config['MAX_CONTENT_LENGTH'] = 16*1024*1024 (16 MiB). Oversized uploads get a clean JSON 413 via an errorhandler. ffmpeg is now a WEB RUNTIME dependency (convert runs in-request), and the web process needs WRITE access to the queue dir -- relevant to systemd/vsmp-web.service hardening (ReadWritePaths=<queue>) and DEPLOY-WEB.md.
- QUEUE_PATH = os.environ.get('VSMP_QUEUE', vsmp.QUEUE_DIR): the SAME dir the player reads. One env var (VSMP_QUEUE) must configure BOTH processes. Still no lock, no DB.
- generate_queue_name() -> '{ms:013d}_{counter:06d}_{rand6}.png' (ms since epoch, per-process threadsafe counter, 6 hex random). Lexical sort == arrival order == FIFO the player drains. Uploaded filename is never trusted/reused (secure_filename only used to label the .incoming temp).
- list_queue_summary(queue_path) -> {names, length, wait_seconds, wait_minutes}. THE single shared wait formula: wait_seconds = length * vsmp.FRAME_INTERVAL_S (150s). Both GET /upload and GET /queue.json use it. Counts only <queue>/*.png via vsmp.list_queue (never .incoming/ or .showing/). Unlocked live snapshot by design.
- Routes: GET /upload (landing+form), POST /upload (endpoint name 'upload_post'; url_for('upload') resolves to the GET endpoint, same /upload path, so the form posts correctly), GET /queue.json, plus the pre-existing GET /, /status.json, /healthz.
- POST /upload flow: require form field named 'image' (clean 400 if missing/empty); save raw upload to <queue>/.incoming/<name>.raw-<hint>; vsmp.convert_image_to_panel_png(raw, <queue>/.incoming/<name>.tmp) [REAL ffmpeg, validates by output not extension/MIME]; os.rename the .tmp into <queue>/<generated>.png (atomic publish, same fs); a finally block always unlinks the raw + any leftover .tmp. On any convert failure -> 400, NOTHING published, temps cleaned. Landed position = 1-based index of the new name in the freshly sorted queue (falls back to 1 if the player already claimed it).
- @app.before_request require_upload_secret(): DISABLED unless env VSMP_UPLOAD_SECRET is set; then it requires an X-Upload-Secret header or a 'secret' form/query field (constant-time compare, else 403). This is the single hook to harden for any non-LAN exposure (design doc section 6).
- webapp.py imports vsmp ONLY (read helpers + convert_image_to_panel_png) and werkzeug.utils.secure_filename; it never imports the epd driver (verified).

Templates/CSS:
- templates/upload.html (NEW): status-card layout, reuses card/facts/muted/small/state classes. Both explainers live in the template (what the VSMP is; how the queue/upload works incl. grayscale+letterbox+never-interrupts+movie-resumes-when-empty). Form: method=post, action=url_for('upload'), enctype=multipart/form-data, <input type=file name=image accept='image/*' required>, NO capture= attribute. Shows queue length + estimated wait in minutes ('about N.N min'); when empty shows 'Queue is empty - the movie is playing' (zero count and message agree). Lists current queue positions. After upload shows ordinal landed-position confirmation ('Added 4th in line'). Links back to status (/) and to /queue.json.
- templates/status.html: added an 'add an image' link (url_for('upload')) in the footer.
- static/style.css: added small .upload (flex form + pill button) and .queue-list rules; everything else reuses existing classes.

tests/test_webapp.py added and registered in tests/run.py MODULES. Uses webapp.app.test_client() with VSMP_QUEUE set to a temp dir under the module work dir BEFORE importing webapp. Conversion is REAL ffmpeg. Covers JPEG+PNG+HEIC (HEIC skips cleanly when sips absent), non-image rejection + missing-field 400 negative controls, empty-queue wording, /queue.json shared formula, and a threaded concurrent-upload check with a background scanner proving queue/*.png never shows a partial/temp file mid-publish.
